text:
sara: FYI ran the 10k qps soak on staging after the kernel-selector tweak. seeing a ~11-13% tail latency regression on host-side for short chat requests. not huge but consistent.

matt: ugh. image? trace? which stack (grpc/http)?

sara: primarily grpc streaming. baseline (old selector) p95 ~72ms, new selector p95 ~81ms. p99 went from 210ms -> 235ms. CPU flat, but host-side syscalls went up in perf samples.

jon: did you profile tokenize/parse? my hunch is extra memcpy or different kernel change causing smaller micro-batches and more framing overhead.

sara: ran perf top and a short flame; hotspots show: tokenize_parse() up ~35% of samples, framer_writev() up ~18%, grpc_writev_hotpath ~12%. KV cache hit rate identical. batching heuristic stats show avg batch size dropped from 6.2 -> 5.1 for <64-token requests.

alice: that drop in batch size could explain per-token overhead increase. sounds like selector change nudged kernel choice for short sequences, increasing per-request scheduling.

matt: can you paste the short perf log? also any socket-level writev counts?

sara: pasted snippet below:

```
# perf sample (shortened)
35.2% tokenize_parse
17.8% framer_writev
12.1% grpc_writev_hotpath
6.3% kvcache_lookup
4.5% kernel_selector_choose
... rest
```

sara: writev counts per-second jumped ~22% on ingress proxy when under heavy multiplexing.

jon: interesting that kvcache_lookup isn't the main culprit. i'd rather optimize host framing + batching. two quick proposals: 1) tweak batching heuristic to prefer bumping up short-seq batch target by +1 if avg seq < 64, 2) coalesce small writev payloads for grpc streaming on same connection for 10ms window.

alice: +1 on coalesce. we already have a micro-coalesce flag for http path; grpc path lacks it. risk: adds 10ms micro-tail to first token. tradeoff looks worth it for 1-2 token prompts.

matt: can we simulate change 1 only (batch target bump) in canary and run soak? cheaper and reversible.

sara: spun a canary with batch target bias +1 for seq<64 on two hosts. quick run: avg batch size recovered to 5.9, p95 returned to ~73ms, p99 down to 212ms. CPU unchanged.

jon: good signal. do we want to ship heuristic bump as short-term fix and follow up on grpc writev coalescing for stable improvement?

alice: agree. add an AB test flag to measure impact across client types (mobile vs web). also create a small perf unit test that asserts avg batch size not drop below 5 for our short-seq workload.

matt: i'll open the PR for heuristic bump and add rollout plan with kill switch. assign to @sara for monitoring dashboards and regression alerts.

infra-bot: deploy requested: canary/ingress-batch-bias -> 2 hosts. CI passed. scheduled 3m rollout. :rocket:

sara: monitoring dashboards updated (route: /dash/ingress/shortseq). alert: p95 delta > 5ms triggers incident. will watch for next 30m.

jon: follow-up task: file an issue to investigate kernel-selector decision tree for short sequences; looks like it picks a kernel with lower throughput but worse host overhead for 1-8 token heads.

alice: filing issue now, tag: eng-runtime, priority: P2.

matt: nice triage team. if canary is good after 30m we roll to 25% then full. documented rollback steps in the PR. :thumbsup:
